items.title: 10-K and 10-Q sections and risk-factor diff
items.evidence: Done: year-over-year risk-factor comparison of the two newest 10-Ks (Item 1A), by code with no model (core `riskfactors.ts`, rules riskdiff-1). New table annual_sections (RLS, owner read), weekly job massive-sections (stocks only; vendor gaps listed, not hidden), panel on the company page that loads the two reports only when opened. Sentence level because page breaks cut paragraphs differently each year; added, removed and edited sentences with the heading each sat under, word-level edits marked by underline and strikethrough (not colour alone), link to each filing. Verified: 33 core tests (hand-checked Dice values, threshold boundaries, page-break joins) mutation-checked; every added, removed and changed sentence of the real pair identical to an independent Python implementation (hash match, 71 new, 49 removed, 66 edited, 449 unchanged); Node and Deno byte-identical; 5 adapter tests and 4 job tests; 2 e2e tests with the real reports. Live 2026-11-24: migration applied; the first job run failed on a rate limit (OKLO) and was recorded as an error, the cause (request bucket burst) was fixed, and the rerun stored 19 reports for 10 companies (RGTI has only one year). The company page also carries a 'Not built' placeholder for 10-Q sections, with the reason (the vendor's sections feed is 10-K only).

items.title: Earnings history: reported results, release timing and post-earnings move (estimates, surprise, guidance and implied move need paid data)
items.evidence: packages/core/src/earnings.ts (formula version earnings-1): each reported quarter (SEC facts) is joined to its Item 2.02 8-K (the latest quarter that ended before the release, at most 95 days earlier; the filing date of a figure is not used because prior-year quarters are repeated in later filings), the release is labelled before the open, during the session or after the close in ET, and the move is the close of the first session that could trade on it against the close before (split-window guard, over-25% flag, bar-gap guard). Every gap is stated in words (no 8-K stored, before the first stored price, reacting session not yet priced, split in window). The summary gives the average size with n, up and down counts and a small-sample warning below 30 reports. Estimates, surprise, guidance and the implied move show 'requires a higher Massive plan' or 'needs options data'. 26 core tests with hand-checked arithmetic (-22.5, +10, +20, +5, -23.08), winter and summer time edges at 09:29:59, 09:30:00, 15:59:59 and 16:00:00 ET, mutation-checked (every mutation applied and caught; five survived the first tests and each got a test). Two design bugs found by checking, not by the first tests: same-day releases were ordered by accession instead of acceptance time, and a prior-year quarter with a later 'filed' date stole the release. Node and Deno output is byte-identical (parity script now covers it). 1 e2e test on the page; screenshot reviewed. Known limit: only 8-Ks the SEC job stored are used (its 'recent' list), so older quarters say 'No results 8-K stored for this quarter' until older submission files are loaded (docs/IDEAS.md).

phases.title: Rules engine, backtest lab and playbooks

Changing future data never changes past signals
Same seed gives identical output

items.title: Rule DSL and evaluator in core
items.evidence: rule-dsl-1 (ADR 0016): JSON rule documents (entry, exit, stop by percent or ATR, time stop; all, any, not; comparisons and crosses of bar fields, sma, ema, highest, lowest, return, rsi, atr, rvol and products), a validator with readable messages, canonical form and content hash for versions, and an evaluator that reads only completed bars. Hand-checked cases; a property test changes every bar after 50 random cut points and finds no earlier signal changed; mutation-checked (one survivor found, test added). Node and Deno identical.

items.title: Seeded playbook library with evidence ratings and sources
items.evidence: ADR 0018: the brief's eleven playbooks with ratings, sources, horizons and summaries; three expressed as rule-dsl-1 rules (index trend filter, ETF time-series momentum, trend-template breakout), the other eight with the exact reason they cannot be tested yet; the leave-out list with reasons; shown on the Lab page. Tests check numbering, sources, rule validity and reasons.

items.title: Point-in-time backtester with costs
items.evidence: backtest-1 (ADR 0017): next-open entries, intrabar stops (gap fills at the open), exit and time stops at the next open, one position at a time, costs per side (commission, slippage, FX). Hand-checked cases and an independent Python backtester on 600 seeded bars (14 trades, one stop) match exactly; look-ahead test: changing bars after a cut never changes an earlier closed trade; mutation-checked (two survivors found, tests added).

items.title: Walk-forward and out-of-sample holdout
items.evidence: Anchored walk-forward folds and a final 20% holdout (ADR 0017): best training Sharpe chosen per fold, only test-window trades count, holdout computed only when revealed and with the last chosen variant; tests check fold order, no leakage into the holdout, and the reveal flag.

items.title: Bootstrap intervals, trial counting, deflated Sharpe
items.evidence: stats-1 (ADR 0016) plus trial counting: walk-forward counts every variant as a trial for the deflated Sharpe ratio, and each stored backtest run records its trial count (backtest_runs.trials).

items.title: Benchmark and regime breakdowns, Monte Carlo drawdowns
items.evidence: backtestReport (ADR 0017): buy-and-hold benchmark over the same dates, regime breakdown at the signal date (values only from 30 trades), Monte Carlo maximum drawdowns from 1,000 seeded resamples (median and worst 5%); same seed identical, another seed changes only the simulations.

items.title: Rule lifecycle
items.evidence: ADR 0018: pure gates (backtested: 30 out-of-sample trades, positive expectancy, 90% interval above zero; live: 20 trading days and 15 shadow signals; demoted: last 30 live signals below the backtest's lower bound) and allowed moves; rules table where a trigger refuses any change to a version's content (RLS test), rule_events log; the runner moves drafts only when the gate passes and never touches live rules (job test).

items.title: GitHub Actions runners
items.evidence: backtest-lab.yml (Sundays 06:20 UTC and by hand): new version only on a changed content hash, walk-forward backtests on stored bars, runs stored with parameters, costs, seed and trial count. Job tests for versioning, live rules untouched, and short histories skipped.

items.title: Replay mode
items.evidence: replayDay (ADR 0018): re-runs a rule on stored bars up to one date and lists each comparison with its values; matches the evaluator on every tested day and is unchanged when later bars change.
